Name: Marriage Overhaul
Author: TitanmasterRy
Description:
[center][size=6][b][color=#e8c882]Marriage Overhaul[/color][/b][/size][/center]
[center][color=#c8a96e]Married life with a pulse.[/color][/center]

[line]

[center][size=4][b]Overview[/b][/size][/center]

Vanilla marriage goes quiet fast. Your spouse becomes furniture that says the same three lines forever. [b]Marriage Overhaul[/b] changes that. Your spouse has moods, gets jealous, expects to be fed, remembers your anniversary, leaves love letters, helps around the farm, gets sick, picks fights when neglected, and slowly builds a real shared history with you.

Every system is [b]individually toggleable[/b] via [b]config.json[/b] and [b]GMCM[/b]. All 12 vanilla spouses have personalized dialogue, and any modded spouse — including those from Stardew Valley Expanded — falls back to a natural generic pool so nothing breaks regardless of your setup.

[line]

[center][size=4][b]Core Systems[/b][/size][/center]

[color=#e8c882][b]Feeding[/b][/color]
Each day is either a cooking day (your spouse handles dinner) or a provides day (they expect food left in the fridge). Forget on a provides day and they go to bed hungry — −40 friendship and a grumpy morning. Leave something and earn +15.

[color=#e8c882][b]Arguments[/b][/color]
When friendship dips below the configured threshold, an argument can break out in the evening. It plays out as a dialogue tree — good responses recover +50, poor ones cost an extra −80. Every vanilla spouse has at least three unique, in-character argument scenarios that rotate so the same one never repeats back to back.

[color=#e8c882][b]Divorce Warning & Auto-Divorce[/b][/color]
Let things slide too far and your spouse mails an in-character warning letter. Ignore it for several consecutive days and they will initiate divorce automatically, with a personalized farewell scene.

[color=#e8c882][b]Jealousy[/b][/color]
Gift someone your spouse considers a rival and they may notice — −15 friendship and an earful the next morning. Odds are higher if the gift was a loved item.

[color=#e8c882][b]Mood System[/b][/color]
Each day your spouse is Happy, Neutral, or Grumpy — shaped by recent friendship trends, feeding, arguments, weather, and a bit of randomness. Mood is expressed through their dialogue and portrait. You only know by talking to them.

[color=#e8c882][b]Anniversary[/b][/color]
Your wedding date is remembered every year. Gift your spouse that day for +200 friendship and a special scene. Forget and face −100 and a disappointed morning.

[color=#e8c882][b]Makeup Gifts[/b][/color]
After a bad argument, your spouse wants to reconcile — they hint at a category of gift (something sweet, something from nature, something homemade). Give the right kind for +150 and reconciliation. Regular gifts give half the usual friendship until you do.

[line]

[center][size=4][b]Extended Systems[/b][/size][/center]
[center][i]17 optional systems, each individually toggleable under the [b]Extended Systems[/b] config section.[/i][/center]

[list]
[*][b]Relationship Milestones[/b] — Special one-time scenes on your 1st, 3rd, and 5th anniversary.[/*]
[*][b]Spouse Chores[/b] — Your spouse may water crops, ship animal products, cook, leave gold, or gather forage. Chance and quality scale with hearts and mood.[/*]
[*][b]Evolving Preferences[/b] — After a year together, they develop new gift preferences tied to your shared history.[/*]
[*][b]Sickness[/b] — Once a season they may fall ill and need soup, medicine, or tea.[/*]
[*][b]Inside Jokes[/b] — Shared moments accumulate and resurface naturally in casual dialogue.[/*]
[*][b]Achievement Pride[/b] — They react to your big wins: mines, Skull Cavern, Community Center, Perfection, legendary fish, skill mastery.[/*]
[*][b]Children Interactions[/b] — References, a weekly time-with-the-kids request, and sharper arguments when little ones are home.[/*]
[*][b]Romantic Letters[/b] — Handwritten love letters in your mailbox, each written in your spouse's voice.[/*]
[*][b]Seasonal Affection[/b] — Every spouse has a favorite and a least-favorite season.[/*]
[*][b]Bad Days[/b] — Sometimes they just struggle. Comforting them matters.[/*]
[*][b]Birthday System[/b] — Your spouse spoils you on your birthday. Set your birthday in config; leave day at 0 to disable.[/*]
[*][b]Town Gossip[/b] — Townsfolk mention how your spouse talks about you around town.[/*]
[*][b]Honeymoon Phase[/b] — The first weeks of marriage are extra sweet.[/*]
[*][b]Spouse Requests[/b] — Mailed requests to fulfill within a few days.[/*]
[*][b]Shared Dreams[/b] — Wake to a journal entry about a dream they had of you.[/*]
[*][b]Visitor Jealousy[/b] — A dry comment when other NPCs linger around the farm.[/*]
[*][b]Productivity Scaling[/b] — A happier spouse is a more helpful one.[/*]
[/list][line]

[center][size=4][b]Cheating[/b][/size]
[size=2][color=#888888]Optional — off by one simple toggle[/color][/size][/center]

Let things deteriorate far enough and your spouse may have an affair with another single villager, and [b]leave you[/b]. It is intentionally harsh. A single toggle in config disables it entirely if it is not for you. The friendship threshold and daily affair chance are both configurable.

[line]

[center][size=4][b]Console Commands[/b][/size][/center]

Console commands are [b]disabled by default[/b]. To enable them, set [b]EnableDebugCommands[/b] to [b]true[/b] in config.json and restart the game. Commands are then accessible through the SMAPI console window.

[b]Available commands:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]mo_status[/b] — Prints your spouse's current mood, friendship, hunger state, and active flags.[/*]
[*][b]mo_argue[/b] — Forces an argument to trigger that evening.[/*]
[*][b]mo_makeup[/b] — Puts your spouse into the makeup-gift state.[/*]
[*][b]mo_hungry[/b] — Sets your spouse as unfed for the day.[/*]
[*][b]mo_jealousy[/b] — Triggers a jealousy reaction.[/*]
[*][b]mo_warn[/b] — Sends the divorce warning letter immediately.[/*]
[*][b]mo_anniversary[/b] — Triggers the anniversary scene for today.[/*]
[*][b]mo_mood <mood>[/b] — Sets your spouse's mood. Valid values: Happy, Neutral, Grumpy.[/*]
[*][b]mo_hearts <n>[/b] — Sets your spouse's friendship to the specified heart value.[/*]
[*][b]mo_cheat[/b] — Forces the cheating and affair event.[/*]
[/list][i]These commands are intended for testing and exploring content. It is recommended to keep [b]EnableDebugCommands[/b] set to false during normal playthroughs.[/i]

[line]

[center][size=4][b]Requirements & Installation[/b][/size][/center]

[b]Requirements[/b]
[list]
[*]Stardew Valley [b]1.6+[/b][/*]
[*][url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url] [b]3.18.0+[/b][/*]
[*](Optional) [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] — configure every system in-game with tooltips[/*]
[/list][b]Installation[/b]
[list=1]

[*]Unzip this mod into your [b]Stardew Valley/Mods[/b] folder.[/*]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[*](Optional) Install GMCM to configure everything in-game.[/*]
[/list][line]

[center][size=4][b]Configuration[/b][/size][/center]

Every system can be toggled and tuned via [b]config.json[/b] or the in-game [b]GMCM[/b] menu. Options are organized under [b]Systems[/b], [b]Thresholds[/b], and [b]Jealousy[/b] sections, each with a tooltip explaining what it does.

Key options and their defaults:
[list]
[*][b]ArgumentThresholdHearts[/b] (default: 10) — Friendship level in hearts below which arguments can trigger.[/*]
[*][b]DivorceWarningThresholdHearts[/b] (default: 8) — Friendship level below which the warning letter is sent.[/*]
[*][b]ConsecutiveDaysBeforeAutoDivorce[/b] (default: 7) — Days below the warning threshold before auto-divorce fires.[/*]
[*][b]CheatingThresholdHearts[/b] (default: 4) — Friendship level below which a neglected spouse may cheat.[/*]
[*][b]CheatingChance[/b] (default: 0.25) — Daily chance the affair triggers while below the threshold.[/*]
[*][b]JealousyChance[/b] (default: 0.20) — Chance the spouse notices a gift to a rival.[/*]
[*][b]JealousyChanceLoved[/b] (default: 0.40) — Chance the spouse notices when the gift was a loved item.[/*]
[*][b]EnableDebugCommands[/b] (default: false) — Enables the mo_* console commands for testing.[/*]
[/list][line]

[center][size=4][b]Compatibility[/b][/size][/center]

[color=#e8c882][b]Modded Spouses — SVE, Custom NPCs[/b][/color]
All 12 vanilla spouses have fully personalized content. Any modded spouse falls back to a natural generic dialogue pool. Nothing breaks; they simply won't have spouse-specific lines until dedicated support is added. SVE personalized dialogue is planned.

[color=#e8c882][b]Helpful Spouses and Chore Mods[/b][/color]
If you use a mod that already handles spouse chores, disable [b]Spouse Chores[/b] and [b]Productivity Scaling[/b] in config to avoid overlap.

[color=#e8c882][b]Children Mods[/b][/color]
Compatible with mods that modify children such as Immersive Family. If issues arise, disable [b]Enable Children Interactions[/b] in config — everything else continues working normally.

[color=#e8c882][b]Modded Farmhouses and Custom Kitchens[/b][/color]
If your farmhouse mod places the fridge in a non-standard location, enable [b]Feeding: Search Extra Storage[/b] in config. This extends detection to mini-fridges and cellar fridges and covers most custom house layouts.

[color=#e8c882][b]Dialogue and Marriage Expansion Mods[/b][/color]
The mod is largely additive and built on vanilla systems. It plays nicely with most dialogue and marriage mods. The kiss and hug handling specifically preserves the vanilla interaction so mods that react to kissing still work correctly.

[color=#e8c882][b]Known Compatible (or at least semi compatible):[/b][/color] Stardew Valley Expanded (Semi compatible, working on integration atm), Haley Ever After, most dialogue packs, PolySweet/FreeLove, Spouses Cook, Any Krobus + Spouse mods
[color=#e8c882][b]Unknown:[/b][/color] Mods that significantly overhaul the core marriage system. If something conflicts, please report it and I will investigate.

[line]

[center][size=4][b]Multiplayer[/b][/size][/center]

Mostly supported as of [b]v1.5.0[/b]. The host and every farmhand each receive a semi-complete Marriage Overhaul experience for their own spouse, saved independently. (There are still many bugs that I'm working hard to fix)

[b]One requirement:[/b] For a farmhand's progress to persist between days, the [b]host must also have Marriage Overhaul installed[/b]. Save data lives on the host's machine — without it on the host, features work during the session but will not carry over overnight.

[list]
[*]The mod only acts on each player's own spouse.[/*]
[*]Dialogue, dreams, and special scenes wait until the player has control before triggering — nothing interrupts shared morning sequences or freezes other players' screens.[/*]
[/list]If you find a multiplayer issue, please report it in the Bugs tab and note whether you were the host or a farmhand, along with your SMAPI log.

[line]

[center][size=4][b]FAQ[/b][/size][/center]

[b]Q: Can I add this mid-playthrough when I'm already married?[/b]
Yes. It works at any point. Your real in-game wedding date is read automatically, so your anniversary triggers on the correct day even if you married long before installing.

[b]Q: How do I trigger an argument or test other systems without waiting?[/b]
Enable [b]EnableDebugCommands[/b] in config.json, then use the mo_* commands in the SMAPI console. See the Console Commands section above for the full list.

[b]Q: Does it work with SVE spouses?[/b]
Yes. SVE spouses use a natural generic dialogue pool for now. Personalized SVE dialogue is planned — see Planned Features.

[b]Q: Does it work with other modded or custom spouses?[/b]
Yes. Any spouse without personalized content defined falls back to the generic pool and still gets moods, arguments, anniversaries, feeding, and all other systems.

[b]Q: I am using Helpful Spouses or another chore mod. Do I need to change anything?[/b]
It is recommended to disable [b]Spouse Chores[/b] and [b]Productivity Scaling[/b] in config to avoid any overlap.

[b]Q: Feeding does not seem to work with my modded farmhouse.[/b]
Enable [b]Feeding: Search Extra Storage[/b] in config or GMCM. This extends fridge detection to mini-fridges and cellar fridges, covering most custom house layouts.

[b]Q: Does the feeding system check what food I leave, or just whether something is there?[/b]
Currently, any food in the fridge satisfies your spouse — they will be happy regardless of what it is. Spouse-specific food preferences are planned for a future update.

[b]Q: I cannot kiss or hug my spouse anymore.[/b]
Make sure you are on the latest version — this is fixed. Approaching your spouse empty-handed now fires the vanilla kiss first, then shows the morning dialogue after. There is also an [b]Allow Spouse Kiss/Hug[/b] toggle in config if you want to adjust the behavior.

[b]Q: Does it work with mods that change how children behave?[/b]
Yes. If any issues arise, disable [b]Enable Children Interactions[/b] in config and everything else will work normally.

[b]Q: Can I disable the affair and divorce mechanics?[/b]
Yes. [b]EnableCheating[/b] and [b]EnableAutoDivorce[/b] are both individual toggles in config.json and GMCM. You can run the full emotional marriage system with none of the harsh consequences.

[b]Q: Is it safe to remove mid-playthrough?[/b]
Yes. The mod stores its own data separately and builds on vanilla marriage data underneath. Uninstalling simply stops the extra systems — your save is unaffected.

[b]Q: I found a bug or want to suggest a feature.[/b]
Please use the [b]Bugs tab[/b] at the top of this page, or open an issue on [url=https://github.com/TitanmasterRy/MarriageOverhaul]GitHub[/url]. Include a description of what happened, whether you are in single-player or multiplayer, and your SMAPI log from [url=https://smapi.io/log]smapi.io/log[/url].

[line]

[center][size=4][b]Translations[/b][/size][/center]

[b]Marriage Overhaul is fully translatable.[/b] As of v1.6.0, all ~1,400 dialogue lines use SMAPI's translation system. You can localize the entire mod without touching any code. Translations are welcome and will be credited.

[b]How to make a translation:[/b]
Open the mod's [b]i18n[/b] folder and find [b]default.json[/b] — the English source file. Copy it, rename it to your locale code (e.g. [b]es.json[/b] for Spanish, [b]de.json[/b] for German), then translate the text on the right side of each line. Anything left untranslated falls back to English automatically.

[b]What to leave unchanged:[/b]
[list]
[*]The [b]keys[/b] on the left side of each colon — do not rename them.[/*]
[*]Anything inside [b]{curly braces}[/b] — these are filled in at runtime with names and item values.[/*]
[*][b]^ symbols[/b] — these are line breaks inside letters.[/*]
[*]Item names (e.g. "Pumpkin Pie") and gift category words ("sweet", "nature", "homemade") — these are identifiers, not display text, and translating them will break item resolution.[/*]
[/list][b]Supported locale codes:[/b] de, es, fr, hu, it, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, zh

[b]How to submit:[/b]
Post your [b]<locale>.json[/b] in the Posts tab, send a direct message, or open a pull request on [url=https://github.com/TitanmasterRy/MarriageOverhaul]GitHub[/url]. You will be credited by name in the description and changelog. You are also welcome to release your translation as its own Nexus page — link back here and I will link to yours.
